title: Navigate home and back
task: Practice moving between your home directory and a subdirectory without using the file browser.

checks.prompt: After `cd ~`, does `pwd` print your home directory path?
After `cd ..`, does `pwd` show the parent of Documents?

hints.text: ~ always means your home directory, whatever directory you are in now.
.. is the parent of the current directory.

solution: cd ~ && pwd && cd Documents && cd .. && pwd

title: Inspect a directory fully
task: List a directory including hidden files, then sort by size to find the largest file.

checks.prompt: Does `ls -a` reveal `.cairn-hidden-demo` while plain `ls` does not?
With `ls -lahS`, is the largest file at the top?

hints.text: -a shows all entries including dot files; -S sorts by size.
Combine flags: `ls -lahS` is long output, human sizes, all entries, sorted by size.

title: Read and count a sample file
setup:
printf 'cairn is a local-first learning engine
it adapts to your answers
it explains every choice
' > cairn-sample.txt
task: Create the sample file, then view its start, its end, and count its lines.

checks.prompt: Does `head -n 1` print the line about being local-first?

hints.text: head takes lines from the top; tail takes them from the bottom.
`wc -l` counts newline characters, so it reports lines.

solution: head -n 1 cairn-sample.txt && tail -n 1 cairn-sample.txt && wc -l cairn-sample.txt

title: Hunt TODOs in a small tree
setup:
printf 'def load():
    # TODO validate input
    return data
' > cairn-demo/src/app.py

printf '# notes

some text without markers
' > cairn-demo/notes.txt
task: Search the whole cairn-demo tree for TODO markers, case-insensitively, with line numbers.

checks.prompt: Does the output show src/app.py with the TODO line and its line number?

hints.text: -r searches directories, -i ignores case, -n prints line numbers.
The pattern comes before the path: `grep -rni todo cairn-demo`.

title: Build a word-frequency pipeline
setup:
printf 'the shell is quiet
the shell is honest
quiet tools last
' > cairn-pipe.txt
task: Count how often each word appears, most frequent first, keeping only the top lines.
commands: cat cairn-pipe.txt | tr ' ' '\n' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 5

checks.prompt: Does the output list words with counts, starting with the word 'the' at 3?
After running it again with `> counts.txt`, does the file exist with the same content?

hints.text: Each stage does one job: split into words, sort, count neighbours, sort numerically, keep the top.
The order matters: uniq only collapses adjacent lines, so sort first.

solution: cat cairn-pipe.txt | tr ' ' '\n' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 5 > counts.txt

title: Build and move a mini project
task: Create a two-level project, copy it, then rename the copy.

checks.prompt: Does `ls -R project` show src and docs with main.py inside src?
Does `ls` show a directory named archive and no project-backup?

hints.text: mkdir -p creates nested directories in one command.
Copying a directory needs cp -r; renaming is just mv with a new name.

solution: mkdir -p project/src project/docs && touch project/src/main.py && cp -r project project-backup && mv project-backup archive

title: Find and size log files
task: Find every .log file under cairn-logs, then list only the files (not directories).

checks.prompt: Does the first find list both app.log files, including the one inside old?
Does `-type f` hide the directories from the output?

hints.text: find needs a starting directory: `find cairn-logs ...`.
Quote the pattern so the shell does not expand it: -name "*.log".

title: Make a script executable
task: Try to run the script, add execute permission, and run it again.

checks.prompt: Before chmod, does running ./greet.sh fail with permission denied?
After chmod +x, does ls -l show an x in the permissions (like -rwxr--r--)?

hints.text: The error message before chmod names the missing permission.
chmod +x adds execute for owner, group, and others at once.
